title: Adaptive retention scheduler and evidence snapshotting for prompts, responses, request-logs and metrics
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: Build an adaptive retention scheduler that enforces per-tenant and per-route retention policies for prompts, model responses, request logs, and derived metrics, with an automated evidence-snapshot pipeline for audits. This ticket defines scope, success criteria, and rollout strategy for a system that supports: (1) policy tiers (hot/nearline/cold) with automatic movement and optional redaction hooks, (2) sample-based long-term metrics aggregation to limit cardinality and storage, (3) evidence snapshot bundles (signed manifests) for compliance review and export, and (4) residency-aware placement so data and evidence exports respect tenant region settings. The scheduler should integrate with existing routing and storage layers (S3-compatible coldstore, nearline Redis clusters, hotstore TTL buckets) and emit proofs-of-deletion and snapshot manifests to the Console and to per-tenant audit logs.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create per-tenant retention policies with: scope (prompt/response/log/metric), tier mapping (hot/nearline/cold), retention windows, and redaction rules via the Console and API.
System moves records between tiers automatically according to configured schedules without downtime; movement events are visible in Console timelines and logged to per-tenant audit trails.
Long-term metrics can be configured to use reservoir sampling or aggregated rollups; sample rate and aggregation window are configurable per-route.

Evidence snapshot: operators can trigger a snapshot for a tenant/date range; snapshot produces a signed manifest, list of included object keys, and optional encrypted export bundle and appears in Console Downloads with proof-of-creation.

Residency enforcement: data never moves to a region outside the tenant residency configuration; scheduler respects region affinity and fails safely with clear error messages if capacity constraints prevent movement.
Proof-of-deletion receipts are generated after permanent deletion and are stored for the tenant's compliance window.
APIs and Console surfaces have feature-flag gating for gradual rollout; telemetry for scheduler actions (counts, latencies, failures) is available to the infra team.
Automated end-to-end test harness validates movements, redaction, evidence snapshot integrity, and residency logic in staging before production rollout.
comments: 2026-02-18: Kickoff meeting — aligned on scope with Eng, Security, and Design. Agreed to build as a modular scheduler service that can be reused by Dedicated and Private deployments.

2026-02-22: Design doc posted: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMMS/pages/retention-scheduler-design. Key call: prefer signed manifests instead of exporting raw logs for initial MVP to reduce exposure.

2026-02-25: Engineering spike complete — prototype demonstrates movement between hotstore and coldstore with S3 lifecycle hooks. Spike notes: github.com/redwood/retention-spikes/poc-archiving (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/2104).

2026-02-28: Security review feedback: require KMS envelope encryption for export bundles, and retention policy audit trails must be immutable for 90 days (security-approved). Security requested one follow-up for HSM integration on Private deployments.

2026-03-01: UX first pass: Console wireframes for policy editor and snapshot download flow in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/retention-policy-editor. Design note: consolidate per-route and per-tenant views to reduce cognitive load.

2026-03-02: Implementation plan: (1) API + policy store, (2) scheduler worker + movement engine, (3) evidence snapshot exporter, (4) Console + telemetry dashboards. Plan to feature-flag region-aware enforcement behind 'retention-residency' flag.
